A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decision-theoretic explanation-evaluation framework. Their text, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v1 Appendices A–B and v2 Appendices A–F.

before.justification: V1 reports an original Ames housing analysis using XGBoost, SHAP and simulated human predictions, with numerical value estimates and confidence intervals (Examples 10/12 and Appendix B).

after.justification: V2 reports medical-data experiments, original reanalyses of earlier human studies, and an alignment-audit experiment with simulated decision-makers (Sections 3–5 and Appendix F).

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes from repeatedly halving signal bins to jointly searching explanation and feature clusters, preserving garbling relationships and maximizing rational-agent payoff. Compared with v1 Appendix A, v2 Appendix C changes the estimator's objective, constraints and procedure.

E1.justification: The Ames housing experiment is removed. V2 evaluates cardiac dysfunction using MIMIC-IV/MIMIC-CXR, hotel-review deception, Amazon Books and Beer sentiment, and training-bias detection using Jigsaw toxic comments. These substantially broaden and replace the evaluated domains and tasks.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates SHAP alongside feature/model signal combinations. V2 adds evaluated comparisons involving LIME and factual/counterfactual medical examples, deception example/heatmap/random-heatmap conditions, expert/top-1/top-2/adaptive sentiment explanations, and SAE explanation variants with a no-explanation control.

E3.justification: V1's housing experiment uses an 80/20 split, linear simulated human predictions and MAPE. V2 introduces accuracy and biopsy-utility evaluations, retrospective human-study analyses, reconstructed deception explanations, rule-based clinical actions and Qwen3-14B simulated auditors. These are new evaluation designs, not same-setting reruns.

E4.justification: V1's housing signal-combination analysis is removed. V2 adds a focused SAE feature-count sensitivity analysis: theoretical value saturates around three features while behavioral effects continue increasing through five (Figure 3 and Table 2). Appendix D supplies formal robustness definitions rather than reported robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals. V1 Figure 1 specifies t-distribution intervals, whereas v2 Figure 2 specifies bootstrap intervals with 1,000 resamples; v2 also reports treatment-effect intervals in Tables 1–2. This changes uncertainty estimation without documenting increased independent runs or seeds.

E6.justification: The housing results disappear and substantial new results are reported. Examples include medical theoretic value approximately 0.12, deception Heatmap treatment effect 0.10 [0.07, 0.13], and SAE-top-5 effect 0.04 [0.03, 0.05] (v2 Sections 3/5 and Tables 1–2). These are different-task findings, not performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds independent/contextual value decompositions and a Blackwell/V-shaped-scoring-rule robustness formulation (Appendix D). It replaces Gaussian-perturbed beliefs with stochastic-kernel garbling (Appendix E) and drops v1's coarsening approximation guarantee. The original no-additional-information proof is retained in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The task-dependent, means-to-an-end thesis and three principal value notions remain. The abstract and introduction shift the claimed contribution toward empirical estimators and demonstrated human-AI/mechanistic-interpretability evaluation, replacing v1's emphasis on general use-case formalization, including recourse and debugging.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of contrasting deception/sentiment effects and SAE information saturation versus behavioral underuse. It discusses accounting for unobserved human private information. Conversely, v1 Section 5's explicit applicability limits concerning future-based and individualized decisions are removed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies task-specific data-construction and explanation procedures, clustering grids and tolerances, an 8,192-unit SAE, Qwen3-14B identification, and full prompt templates (Appendix F), replacing the housing implementation details. It also adds an OSF code/data access link.

R1.justification: V2 adds explicit positioning against Chen et al.'s use-case-grounded simulations and connects the framework to pragmatic interpretability, mechanistic auditing and scoring-rule research. It substantially replaces v1's Alternative Views discussion, including cited critiques of conventional decision theory, rather than merely updating references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 reorganizes the framework around estimands, estimation and demonstrations, moves the existing proof and bounded-agent discussion into appendices, and changes terminology, title and author ordering.

P2.justification: The single-column main text becomes two-column with redesigned example boxes. The housing bar chart is removed; v2 adds a workflow diagram, embedded medical payoff plots, multipanel human-study/audit figures and two treatment-effect tables.

improvement.justification: V1 empirically illustrates the framework only through synthetic housing decisions. V2 substantially strengthens practical validation by relating theoretical benchmarks to observed human-study behavior, revising the estimator and supplying richer implementation details. Reconstructed deception explanations, simulated clinical/audit decisions and removal of broader applicability caveats limit the gains, but the framework's empirical grounding and usability improve substantially.
